title: Feature Engineering
description: Transform raw data into meaningful, informative features for machine learning models.
content:
**Feature engineering** is the process of transforming raw data into a set of meaningful, informative, and non-redundant features that can be effectively used by machine learning algorithms.

The quality of features often matters as much as the choice of the model itself: even a powerful algorithm will struggle if it receives raw, messy, or uninformative inputs.

> Feature engineering can be broken down into four key aspects:
> • Preprocessing
> • Transformation
> • Construction
> • Extraction

**Preprocessing** is the first step: before any transformation, the raw data often requires cleaning (e.g., handling missing values, smoothing noisy data, correcting inconsistencies). Preprocessing might include different techniques to prepare data for further transformations.

**Transformation** is needed because raw features may not directly fit the assumptions or structure required by models. This stage involves normalization, standardization, log- or power-transformation, encoding techniques, etc.

**Construction** is the process of creating new features by combining or aggregating existing ones. Such features can reveal hidden relationships - this step leverages domain knowledge to introduce features that might capture complex patterns more simply. For example, from a single "purchase date" column one can construct features like "day of the week" or "days since last purchase".

**Extraction** involves reducing the dimensionality of the data while retaining most of its information. Techniques such as PCA or t-SNE can automatically extract features from data. This is especially useful in visual, textual, or audial data scenarios, where the raw input (e.g., pixels or audio samples) is high-dimensional and must be compressed into a smaller set of informative features.
